question.text:
$f$ $Y=2$ $Y=4$
$X=1$ $\dfrac{1}{4}$ $\dfrac{1}{8}$
$X=3$ $\dfrac{1}{2}$ $\dfrac{1}{8}$

Compute $P(X = 3 \,|\, Y = 2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.explanation:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by \[ P(X = 3 \,|\, Y = 2) = \dfrac{P(X = 3 , Y = 2)}{P(Y = 2)} = \dfrac{f(3,2)}{f_Y(2)}, \] where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, \begin{align} f_Y(2) & = f(1,2) + f(3,2) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{4}. \end{align}

From the given table, we have that $f(3,2) = \dfrac{1}{2}.$

Finally, substituting $f_Y(2) = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and $f(3,2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ in our formula above, we obtain \begin{align} P(X = 3 \,|\, Y = 2) & = \dfrac{f(3,2)}{f_Y(2)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{3}. \end{align}

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

\begin{align} f_Y(3) &=f(2,3) + f(4,3) + f(6,3) \\[3pt] &=0.25+0.05+0.15 \\[3pt] &=0.45. \end{align}

question.text:
$f$ $Y=0$ $Y=2$ $Y=4$ $Y=6$
$X=0$ $0.25$ $0.05$ $0.1$ $0$
$X=1$ $0.1$ $0.05$ $0.2$ $0.1$
$X=2$ $0$ $0.1$ $0.05$ $0$

Compute $P(2 \lt Y \leq 6\,|\, X=0 )$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.explanation:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

\begin{align*} P(2 \lt Y \leq 6\,|\, X=0) &= \dfrac{P\big((2\lt Y \leq 6) , X=0\big)}{P(X=0)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P\big(X=0 , (2\lt Y \leq 6) \big)}{P(X=0)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(X=0 , Y=4) + P(X=0 , Y=6)}{P(X=0)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{f(0,4) + f(0,6)}{f_X(0)}, \end{align*}

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

\begin{align} f_X(0) &=f(0,0) + f(0,2) + f(0,4) + f(0,6)\\[3pt] &=0.25 +0.05+0.1+0 \\[3pt] &=0.4. \end{align}

From the given table, we have that $f(0,4)=0.1$ and $f(0,6)=0.$

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain

\begin{align} P(2 \lt Y \leq 6\,|\, X=0 ) &= \dfrac{f(0,4) + f(0,6)}{f_X(0)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.1 + 0}{0.4}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.1}{0.4}\\[5pt] &=0.25. \end{align}

Compute $P(1\leq Y \leq 3\,|\, X=1 )$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

\begin{align*} P(1\leq Y \leq 3\,|\, X=1 ) &= \dfrac{P\big((1\leq Y \leq 3) , X=1\big)}{P(X=1)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P\big(X=1 , (1\leq Y \leq 3) \big)}{P(X=1)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(X=1 , Y=1) + P(X=1 , Y=2) + P(X=1 , Y=3)}{P(X=1)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{f(1,1) + f(1,2)+ f(1,3)}{f_X(1)}, \end{align*}

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

\begin{align} f_X(1) &=f(1,0) + f(1,1) + f(1,2) + f(1,3)\\[3pt] &=0.1 + 0 +0.3 + 0.05 \\[3pt] &=0.45. \end{align}

From the given table, we have that $f(1,1)=0, f(1,2)=0.3$ and $f(1,3)=0.05.$

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain

\begin{align} P(1\leq Y \leq 3\,|\, X=1 ) &= \dfrac{f(1,1) + f(1,2) + f(1,3)}{f_X(1)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0 + 0.3+ 0.05}{0.45}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.35}{0.45}\\[5pt] &\approx 0.78. \end{align}

$X=2$ $\dfrac{1}{8}$ $0$ $\dfrac{5}{16}$
$X=4$ $\dfrac{3}{16}$ $0$ $\dfrac{1}{16}$

Compute $P( 0 \leq Y \lt 10 \,|\, X=4)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.explanation:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

\begin{align*} P( 0 \leq Y \lt 10 \,|\, X=4) &= \dfrac{P\big((0\leq Y \lt 10) , X=4\big)}{P(X=4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P\big(X=4 , (0\leq Y \lt 10)\big)}{P(X=4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(X=4,Y=0) + P(X=4,Y=5)}{P(X=4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{f(4,0) + f(4,5)}{f_X(4)}, \end{align*}

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

\begin{align} f_X(4) &=f(4,0) + f(4,5) + f(4,10)\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{3}{16}+0 + \dfrac{1}{16}\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4}. \end{align}

From the given table, we have that $f(4,0)=\dfrac{3}{16}$ and $f(4,5)=0.$

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain

\begin{align} P( 0 \leq Y \lt 10 \,|\, X=4) &= \dfrac{f(4,0) + f(4,5)}{f_X(4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{16} + 0\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{16}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{4}. \end{align}

Compute $f_{X|Y}(1 \,|\, 2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.explanation:
The conditional probability mass function $f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as \[ f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y=y). \]

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability \[ f_{X|Y}(1 \,|\, 2) = P(X = 1 \,|\, Y = 2). \]

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have \[ P(X = 1 \,|\, Y = 2) = \dfrac{P(X = 1, Y = 2)}{P(Y = 2)} = \dfrac{f(1,2)}{f_Y(2)} \] where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, \begin{align} f_Y(2) & = f(1,2) + f(2,2) + f(3,2) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{7}{32} + \dfrac{5}{32} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align}

From the given table, $f(1,2) = \dfrac{1}{8}.$

Finally, substituting $f_Y(2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $f(1,2) = \dfrac{1}{8}$ in our formula above, we obtain \begin{align} f_{X|Y}(1 \,|\, 2) & = P(X = 1 \,|\, Y = 2) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{f(1,2)}{f_Y(2)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{4}. \end{align}

Compute $f_{Y|X}(0 \,|\, 1)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
The conditional probability mass function $f_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)$ is defined as \[ f_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) = P(Y = y \,|\, X = x). \]

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability \[ f_{Y|X}(0 \,|\, 1) = P(Y = 0 \,|\, X = 1). \]

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have \[ P(Y = 0 \,|\, X = 1) = \dfrac{P(X = 1, Y = 0)}{P(X = 1)} = \dfrac{f(1,0)}{f_X(1)} \] where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_X(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus, \begin{align} f_X(1) & = f(1,0) + f(1,1) + f(1,2)\\[5pt] & = 0.25 + 0.1 + 0.25 \\[5pt] & = 0.6. \end{align}

From the given table, $f(1,0) = 0.25.$

Finally, substituting $f_X(1) = 0.6$ and $f(1,0) = 0.25$ in our formula above, we obtain \begin{align} f_{Y|X}(0 \,|\, 1) & = P(Y = 0 \,|\, X = 1) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{f(1,0)}{f_X(1)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0.25}{0.6} \\[5pt] & \approx 0.42. \end{align}

Compute $f_{X|Y}(0 \,|\, 2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
The conditional probability mass function $f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as \[ f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y=y). \]

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability \[ f_{X|Y}(0 \,|\, 2) = P(X = 0 \,|\, Y = 2). \]

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have \[ P(X = 0 \,|\, Y = 2) = \dfrac{P(X = 0, Y = 2)}{P(Y = 2)} = \dfrac{f(0,2)}{f_Y(2)} \] where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, \begin{align} f_Y(2) & = f(0,2) + f(1,2) \\[5pt] & = 0.15 + 0.25 \\[5pt] & = 0.4. \end{align}

From the given table, $f(0,2) = 0.15.$

Finally, substituting $f_Y(2) = 0.4$ and $f(0,2) = 0.15$ in our formula above, we obtain \begin{align} f_{X|Y}(0 \,|\, 2) & = P(X = 0 \,|\, Y = 2) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{f(0,2)}{f_Y(2)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{0.15}{0.4} \\[5pt] & \approx 0.38. \end{align}
